Business Description:
The view is the Landing page for the Resource Management module. This view will show the key information for a Resource Manager to assess:

3) Staff demand for existing demands.

User Groups:
Resource Manager

User Stories:
1)View Guidance % by Resource. Rolling 12 months (Pivot)
2)Drill into Resource to Resource by Project Guidance view
3)View all Plans created, that have a Status of "Staffing Required".
4)Drill into Plan to Staffing Required Plans view
5)View all Staff requests for existing Demands
6)Drill into Demand Request View

Epics.title: Maintain Applicants (Status, Notes)
Epics.description:
So that I can provide more context to the hiring team to make a decision

Acceptance Criteria
Process should require applicants to progress through each status
If status are skipped, provide a reason why via comment
IE: No Tech Assessment required, Martyn made an executive decision.
From Request Page: Ability to quickly view Applicant info (Notes, Skills, LinkedIn)   
Should see a view of all Applications by Pipeline stage
Should see a count of current Application per Status
Dev notes: Subquery for counts by status
Quick Jump to LinkedIn Profile to study before call.
Add notes specific to the Application

Additional Notes
What happens to all the applicants when a role is moved to “On Hold” or “Completed? Is there a database or somewhere that we can view all applicants tied to a “Closed or On Hold” role? Or a place to view all applicants in general regardless of their status? For ex. if we hire someone for the CSM role and hit “complete” for that particular role request, but I would also like to someday hire someone else tied to that role request, do we just move that entire role back to Open for when we want to hire that other person? I guess what I’m getting at is that I liked having the view of all recruits listed in one place. RIght now, the only view is by role and if we go back to my first point, it can get confusing/disorganized when multiple role requests can be made and information can live in multiple role requests.   
Can we have notes for a specific application?

Epics.title: Add Role Requests
Epics.description:
So that I can Fill Headcount, Grow the Company

Acceptance Criteria
Validation if there is an existing Role Request for the Same Role - while they are both open   
Dev Notes: Potentially add a validation warning if the role request exists and is still active.
Filter Requests by Status
Know how many applications are in each Request Status
Quickly View Applicant Profile, add notes
Leave notes on Role Request
Prioritize Role Request
Specify Target Date "We need this role by end of 2025 Q1"
Status should default to "Open"
Requested on should default, then be updated as needed
System should warn me if I am trying to create a request that already exists (Avoid Dupes)   
Indicator of the number of Requests per status
Requested on, Requested By should default to current time & user, but allowed to be editable.
Required Fields
Request Name
Role
Requested On
Requested by
Priority
Status


Additional Notes
Since we now have the ability to add multiple recruits against a role request, should we limit the ability to request/add for the same exact role? For ex. I was able to add another role request for Trainee App Dev support even though there’s already one existing, and with recruits tied to it. I’m just afraid that it can get disorganized  and we’re adding recruits to either of the two line items and we’re not sure where certain recruit profiles live.   
In the notes section for each role, it would be great if a date is automatically captured with the note. That way, we can quickly see the updated notes and know if they’re outdated or not. For ex. I can see us adding a note saying “need 2 hires for this role” Oct. 10, 2024 and then at a later time, we add another note “We only need 1 now. The other has been fulfilled” Oct 16, 2024. If not, then we can just manually write it in the notes. It would just be a nice to have.

Move Utilization Reports from Demand Planning to Resource Management
Tasks.description:
Process:
Start at the Top level Page and work your way through.
Copying a page requires the pages that it links to via buttons or hyperlinks to be set to shared
(Shared setting is in the edge case of a page)
Try copying a page and it will give you a validation if it has pages it links to that need to be set to shared.
Find pages within that page that are set to Link To (Buttons, Text, etc) and open those. Set those to shared and Copy that page you linked into. then Go back and try again.
Once all pages the top level page links to is set to shared and copied then copy the top level and then change all of the links to be to the new pages created in the Resource Management application

From Melissa

1 deal is tied to 1 plan

Question: Can multiple Plans be tied to 1 demand?

Since we can only tie 1 plan to 1 demand, what should we do with the plan when we’re unable to assign a demand?
Also, if through the same process the change order Plan creates an empty demand.

A change order deal is created.

Change order demands can have a list of plans.

Tasks.description:
Below are requirement for a Resource Manager and HR to assess an employees time allocation over a period of time, across projects, demands, tasks and accounts. The dashboard will help RMs / Mgr figure out future placement for new roles or accounts. Provides the ability to generally assess the persons time and give feedback on better allocation. I don't know where this lives, maybe under resource manage.  A new link called people.

Wire Frames
Filter Panel
Select Person 
Select From Month
Select To Month
Quick Filters for 
Current Year Months and 
Last 6 months (Excluding Current)
Last 3 months (Excluding Current)
Last Month
This Month


Summary Metrics (MRP Tile at the Top), very similar to Team manager view:
Person
Total Utilization - Are they working in general
Client Utilization NEW (Sales + Client Time / Total Capacity) - How client facing are they
Billable Utilization (Billable Hours / Total Capacity) - How billable are they (true billable time)
Weighted Billable Utilization (Billable Hours / Target Hours) - Are they working their target
Weighted Guided Utilization  (Actual Hours / Guided Hours) - Are they working their guidance (NB or Billable)
Time Off Utilization NEW (PTO / Total Capacity) - Are they taking time off
Drill into details of that person retaining the time period filters.

Detail Panels (linked to top Summary MRP)
MRP Panels
Sum by Demands
Sum by Projects
Sum by Accounts
Sum by Parent Tasks
All  Panels have these Columns
Description of the thing (Project, Demand, Parent Task, Account)
Total Hours--> Drill into detail (sustaining filters)
Billable Hours --> Drill into detail (sustaining filters)
Non Billable Hours --> Drill into detail (sustaining filters)

I would like to see a pie chart of 
Trend Chart
By Month, using the filters assigned
Capacity (line)
Guided (Bar)
Actual (Bar)
Actual Billable (Bar)
Bar Chart - Sorted by Total DESC, carrying filters over
Top 10 Accounts sorted DESC by total hours
Bar Chart - Sorted by Total DESC, carrying filters over
Top 10 Parent Tasks, color coded by the above. Drill into child tasks.
Bar Chart - Sorted by Total DESC, carrying filters over
Top 10 Projects (not demands) Time 

Pie Chart - Time Allocation Visual (this would require categorizing all projects can be a later phase):
Sales / Acct Mgmt Time - Blue
Client Projects - Green
Internal Projects - Purple
Dept  or Role Team Time -  Dark Purple
People Mgmt (1on1) - Dark Orange
Recruiting - Light Orange
User Stories
1.	As a Resource Manager, I want to select a person from the left-hand navigation, so that I can monitor individual performance and utilization metrics for targeted resource management.

	2.	As a Resource Manager, I want to filter data by selecting a “From Date” and “To Date,” so that I can analyze trends and performance over specific periods.

	3.	As a Resource Manager, I want to use quick filters for the “Current Year” and the “Last 6 Months,” so that I can easily access recent and relevant utilization metrics without manual input.

	4.	As a Resource Manager, I want to see Total Utilization as a top-level metric, so that I can assess whether team members are fully engaged.

	5.	As a Resource Manager, I want to track Client Utilization (Sales + Client Time / Total), so that I can evaluate how client-facing each resource is and plan accordingly for sales or client engagements.

	6.	As a Resource Manager, I want to monitor Billable Utilization (Billable Hours / Total Capacity), so that I can understand the proportion of time spent on billable activities relative to available capacity.

	7.	As a Resource Manager, I want to review Weighted Billable Utilization (Billable Hours / Target Hours), so that I can track if resources are meeting their billable hour targets.

	8.	As a Resource Manager, I want to see detailed breakdowns in panels such as Projects, Demands, Accounts, and Parent Tasks, so that I can understand where time is being allocated across different work streams.

	9.	As a Resource Manager, I want to drill into Total, Billable, and Non-Billable Hours in the detail panels, so that I can retain filters and gain deeper insights into specific time allocations.

	10.	As a Resource Manager, I want visualizations like trend charts by month, pie charts for time allocation, and bar charts showing top accounts, tasks, and projects, so that I can make data-driven decisions and determine resource placement more effectively.

Tasks.title: Add: Resource Billable Performance Report
Tasks.description:
Report Details:
Past Billable Guidance vs. Actuals:
Billable Guidance: Displays the projected or planned billable hours for each resource (Monthly, possibly weekly)
Billable Actuals: Shows the actual billable hours logged by each resource during these periods
Variance Details: Calculates the difference between the Billable Guidance and Billable Actuals, showcasing whether the resource underperformed, overperformed, or met expectations.
Variance Analysis:
Percentage Variance: Expresses the variance as a percentage to easily see the degree of deviation from the billable guidance
Variance Trends: Tracks how frequently resources either miss or exceed their billable targets, providing insight into patterns over time
Nice To Have: Reasons for large variance between Budget and Actuals
Trend Analysis: recurring patterns of over- or under-performance to inform forecasting accuracy, staffing decisions, and demand planning.
Root Cause Attribution: Capture standardized reasons for material variance (e.g., scope change, client delay, internal reprioritization, ramp-up/down timing).
Budget vs. Actual Commentary: Enables leadership to distinguish controllable vs. non-controllable variance.

Frequency of Missed Targets:
Missed Billable Targets: A metric that shows how often a resource does not hit their billable actuals compared to the guidance, presented as a percentage or count
Contributing Factors: Notes or a breakdown section to document reasons for missed targets, such as project delays, lack of client work, or internal resource reallocation
Report Frequency:
Weekly and Monthly Reporting: The report can be generated weekly for quick course corrections and monthly for more strategic planning and performance reviews.

Tasks.description:
Add:
Currently, users can only assign one individual to an action card at a time. This creates inefficiencies when multiple assignees need the same task, as it requires creating separate action cards for each individual. A multi-select feature for assignees would streamline this process by allowing users to assign multiple individuals to the same action card, automatically generating individual assignments for each assignee.
Details:
In a recent meeting, users identified a task that needed to be assigned to multiple participants.
Without a multi-select option, users had to manually create multiple action cards for the same task.
A multi-select feature would improve efficiency and organization by reducing repetitive manual input.
Steps to Reproduce:
Create a new action card 
Attempt to assign multiple individuals to the action card.
Observe: Only one assignee can be selected at a time.
To assign the same task to multiple individuals, additional action cards must be created manually.
Expected Behavior:
Users can select multiple assignees from a dropdown or list.
The system automatically creates individual assignments for each selected assignee under the same task.
Impact:
Reduces manual work and ensures consistency in task assignments.
Enhances team organization and tracking of responsibilities.
Priority: Normal
Acceptance Criteria:
Multi-select functionality is added to the assignee field.
Individual action cards are automatically created for each selected assignee.
Existing functionality, such as due dates, priority, and status, remains intact.

Tasks.title: Fix: Time Entry Incorrect Mapping
Tasks.description:
Fix
Users are experiencing incorrect mapping when entering time against existing tickets and using the copy feature. Specifically, tasks appear to map incorrectly to a different SOW (e.g., "Client Meetings" mapping to "Sales"). Additionally, when editing an existing time entry, tasks marked as billable in the project task are showing up as non-billable (NB) after changes are made.
 
Steps to Reproduce:
Add a new time entry.
Set Project to MPro | Agency CRM.
Set Task to Client Meetings.
Attempt to copy a time entry or edit an existing entry from a previous week.
Observe:
Incorrect mapping occurs (e.g., "Client Meetings" maps to "Sales" instead).
Edited entries marked as billable default to non-billable (NB).
Expected Behavior:
Tasks should map correctly when entering time or copying a previous entry.
Edited tasks should retain their billable status as defined in the project task.
Impact:
Causes confusion and errors in time tracking, potentially leading to incorrect billing.
Users must re-check and manually correct entries, which reduces efficiency.

Developer Notes:   
Binding Issue: The copy feature may be binding on the title value and picking the top record. Source column TaskID -> target column ProjectTaskID (Type=Shared) appears to be the mapping logic. The issue might occur when the task is edited, and the TaskID becomes locked.
Billable vs. Non-Billable Issue: For non-billable entries, this might occur if the task is edited post sign-off. Need to confirm if sign-off introduces a default behavior of marking tasks as NB.

Resources

Tasks.description:
Criteria:
Send on Schedule (Daily), 10am EST

Mon: Send out reminder for emails due in 3 days (Due on Thu)

Tasks.title: Configure a Send As Distribution List in Azure
Tasks.description:
We dont want emails to go to clients as the noreply@nymbl.app email, rather our AR@nymbl.app address. This will allow emails from our domain, and allow clients to reply to emails send, which would go to our distribution group.

this can be accomplished with the Send As configuration in Azure. 

To send emails as a specified distribution list (DL) using SMTP, you'll need to ensure that the account you're using has the necessary "Send As" permissions for the distribution list. Here are the steps to achieve this:
1. Grant "Send As" Permissions
First, you need to grant "Send As" permissions to the account that will be sending the emails. This can be done through the Exchange admin center:
Open the Exchange Admin Center (EAC):
Go to Recipients > Groups.
Select the distribution group you want to configure.
Under Settings, select Edit manage delegates.
Add the user or service account and set the permission type to Send As[1][2].
2. Configure SMTP Settings
Next, configure your SMTP settings to use the distribution list's email address as the "From" address. Here’s an example configuration:
SMTP Server: smtp.office365.com
Port: 587 (or 25)
Encryption: STARTTLS
Username: your_account@yourdomain.com
Password: your_password
From: distribution_list@yourdomain.com
3. Send Email Using SMTP
Here’s a sample code snippet in Python to send an email using SMTP with the specified "From" address:
import smtplib
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.text import MIMEText

# SMTP server configuration
smtp_server = "smtp.office365.com"
smtp_port = 587
username = "your_account@yourdomain.com"
password = "your_password"

# Email details
from_address = "distribution_list@yourdomain.com"
to_address = "client@example.com"
subject = "Subject of the Email"
body = "Body of the Email"

# Create the email
msg = MIMEMultipart()
msg['From'] = from_address
msg['To'] = to_address
msg['Subject'] = subject
msg.attach(MIMEText(body, 'plain'))

# Send the email
server = smtplib.SMTP(smtp_server, smtp_port)
server.starttls()
server.login(username, password)
server.sendmail(from_address, to_address, msg.as_string())
server.quit()
Additional Resources
Send email as a distribution list
Allow members to send as or send on behalf of a group
If you encounter any issues or need further assistance, feel free to ask! 😊

References
[1] Send email as a distribution list - Microsoft 365 admin
[2] Allow members to send as or send on behalf of a group

Tasks.title: Improve: More Accurate Total Capacity based on Start Date
Tasks.description:
What New Hires are getting total capacity assigned with incorrect totoal capacity
Why Impacts KPIs

Notes
Need to leverage Start Date when calculating Total Capacity
Example: Parker starts on March 11th, so he should not have a full month of hours for March.  
We should calculate based on Start Date
Full Month of March = 21 Working Days * 8 Hours = 168 Hours
Start Date is March 11th, so he will be a FTE for 15 Full Days in March 15*8 = 120
His Total Capacity for March should be 120 Hours, not 168

Tasks.title: Add: All tickets for account page
Add: Section for Technical Assessment Materials
Tasks.description:
Add
A new section to the NOS Talent Mgmt app to centralize and store technical assessment deliverables for candidates.

Why
Currently, there is no standardized location in the Talent Mgmt app to house technical assessments. This makes it difficult for hiring managers, tech partners, and project leads to reference evaluation materials and make informed decisions during staffing.

 
Dev Notes   

Idea: Add this feature with 3 tables.
This way, the recruiting team can start with a template, but customize / add remove as they need .
All of the data would live outside of TM app, but we can use it as a central hub so we don't have to store files.
Example
Link to Video Recording
Link to Slide Deck
Link to Write Up
etc...
We can review on next Dev call  
Dev Notes

New Table: AssetType (Configuration Table)
This is a simple lookup table that lists the allowed types of assets.
You can update this list as needed without changing code.
Fields:
AssetTypeID: a unique ID for the type
Name: the label, like "Technical Assessment", "Recorded Demo", "Final Evaluation"
Description: optional explanation of the type
SortOrder: a number to help sort the list (e.g., in dropdowns)

New Table: AssetTemplate
This table stores reusable templates for common types of assets—like a standard technical evaluation format. (Could also add by Role)
Each row is a reusable pattern that users can pick from when adding an asset.
Fields:
AssetTemplateID: a unique ID for the template
Name: the name of the template
Description: optional info about how/why the template is used
AssetTypeID: what kind of asset this template is for (links to AssetType)
SuggestedTitle: default title when using the template
DefaultDescription: default description when using the template
CreatedByUserID: the user who made the template
CreatedAt: when the template was created

New Table: ApplicantAsset
This table stores technical assessment materials for each applicant, such as recordings, documents, or evaluations.
Each row represents one asset (file or link) related to an applicant.
Fields:
ApplicantAssetID: a unique ID for this asset (UUID)
ApplicantID: the applicant this asset belongs to (links to the Applicant table)
AssetTypeID: the type of asset (links to the AssetType table, e.g., "Demo", "Evaluation")
Title: a short name for the asset
Description: longer optional notes
Url: a link to the file, video, or document
SubmittedByUserID: the user who added this asset (links to the User table)
SubmittedAt: when the asset was added
AssetTemplateID: (optional) links to a template if this asset was created from one@Brian

Tasks.description:
As a Resource Manager I want the ability to create a Demand directly from the Staff Plan Report (via a “Create Demand” button), so that I can initiate the staffing process even before a contract request is submitted to Client Operations.

 Acceptance Criteria
A “Create Demand” button is added to the Staff Plan Report.
Resource Managers can create a Demand when a plan status is set to Ready for Resourcing, even if no contract request exists yet.
Client Operations can also create a Demand when a Contract Request precedes a Resource Plan.
Existing “View Demand” functionality remains intact and is not removed or replaced.

Tasks.title: Add: Automate Client Success Status Updates in Metric Stage
Tasks.description:
User Story
As a MetrycStage Admin
I want to Automate the Client Success Sentiment based on CRM Sentiment
So that I don’t have to manually maintain this KPI
Acceptance Criteria
Client Success Should auto update each month based on CRM Sentiment for the Account
We should track the CSM linked to that account on the time of insert into the History Table
 --

Currently, client success statuses in Metric Stage are being manually updated during account rundown calls. This creates risk of KPI data being out of sync with CRM if updates are missed. Proposal is to automate this update.

Add user ID to client, add the user ID to client history. 
Two update rules. One to have set it and one to unset it
Change the history CRAM to include the user ID

Add Responsible CSM ID to Snapshot
 Capture Person ID (isResponsible) from CRM Account Person (the assigned CSM).
 Ensure this ID is stored in the history snapshot table at the time the snapshot is taken.
 Confirm mapping logic so the correct CSM is tied to the account at snapshot time.
Automate Client Success Flag
 Create an update rule on the CRM Client Table to set the success flag automatically.
 Rule logic:
If CRM sentiment is neutral or negative → set success flag to 0 (unsuccessful).
If CRM sentiment is good, great, or onboarding → set success flag to 1 (successful).
 Replace manual updates in the front-end with this automation.
Validation & Testing
 Verify updates flow correctly into Metric Stage and history tables.
 Test both scenarios (positive sentiment → flag = 1; neutral/negative sentiment → flag = 0).
 Confirm responsible CSM ID is visible in reporting snapshots.

Users can filter the Utilization Report by Pillar.
Historical and new utilization data reflects the correct pillar for each person.

********

A. TRM / NOS – Org Structure & Admin UI

Primary Role support

This can be enforced via:
Unique index on (PersonId) filtered by IsPrimary = 1, or

A3. Admin UI – Page to Manage Pillars, Departments & Roles

Tasks.title: Improve: Adjust Project Guidance Within NOS
Tasks.description:
**For Ticketing App Phase 2

Original Request
This whole process seems odd to me. We need to just make a button in NOS to do this.  I just changed the guidance, told Melissa and the account mgmt channel, and now Marcos is making slack requests.
Should be go to a Demand / Project. Increase / Decrease guidance. Auto approve if they have capacity or budget. If not it routes to RM for approval.
I think it's worth re-visiting this process as it will help optimize revenue and make managing guidance easier.

User Story
As a Project Manager or Account Manager
I want the ability to increase or decrease guidance directly within the NOS Demand/Project screen
So that I can quickly make updates, automatically notify the right stakeholders, and ensure guidance changes follow proper approval workflows without requiring Slack messages or manual communication.
A centralized workflow inside NOS will:
Remove unnecessary Slack noise
Increase speed, accuracy, visibility
Improve revenue tracking and resource planning
Proposed Capability
A “Change Guidance” button within each Demand/Project record that enables:
Direct Increase/Decrease actions
Auto-approval (if budget/capacity allows)
RM review only when necessary
Automated notifications
Auditable history
Acceptance Criteria
1. Guidance Change Action
 A “Change Guidance” button is visible on each Demand/Project.
 Clicking opens a modal with:
Increase or Decrease toggle
Current guidance (read-only)
New guidance field
Reason (free text)
Effective month selector
 Form validates that the new value is numeric and greater than or equal to zero.
2. Automatic Validation & Approval Rules
 System checks remaining budget and capacity.
 If within limits → Auto-approve the change.
 If outside limits → Route to RM for approval.
 RM receives in-app and notification-based tooling to approve/deny.
3. Notifications & Communication
 Auto-notify these groups when a change is approved:
Melissa
Account Management
Resource Management (only when RM intervention was needed)
 Notification includes:
Team Member
Client Name
Demand/SOW
Old Guidance
New Guidance
Month
Reason for change
 Slack or email delivery options configurable.
4. Audit Log
 NOS logs every guidance change:
Timestamp
User
Old → New value
Approval path (auto or RM)
Reason
Demand/Project reference link
5. Permissions
 PMs and Account Managers can submit guidance changes.
 RMs can review/approve guidance changes when necessary.
 Audit logs visible only to authorized roles.
  UI / UX Notes
Change Guidance Button
Should be placed near the existing Guidance section on the Demand/Project detail page.
Styled as a primary or secondary action button for visibility.
Consider using an icon (  or  ) to reinforce the concept of adjusting values.
Modal Layout
Clean, high-contrast form with clear section labeling:
Current Guidance
New Guidance
Reason
Effective Month
Use input constraints (no negative values, only integers).
Provide inline feedback if the change is likely to require RM approval (e.g., “  This change exceeds available capacity and will require RM review.”)
Approval Workflow UX
If auto-approved, the user sees instant confirmation: “Guidance successfully updated.”
If RM approval is required, the modal should update:
“This change has been submitted to Resource Management for review.”
Notifications should be standardized and templated for consistency.
Audit Trail UX
Present audit history as a chronological list inside the Demand/Project page.
Include tooltips to explain approval types (auto vs RM).
Each log entry could support “View Details” for deeper context.
Example Scenario (End-to-End)
Scenario: Increasing Guidance with Auto-Approval
Chris is managing Adeptia SOW #6 for November.
Sophia messages Chris saying they need 10 more hours for support with Allie.
Chris opens the Demand in NOS and clicks Change Guidance.
Modal shows:
Current: 125
New: 135
Reason: “Additional support hours with Allie Chu”
System checks available capacity and budget.
Everything is within limits → Auto-approve.
NOS automatically:
Updates guidance to 135
Logs the change
Sends notifications to Melissa + Account Mgmt
No Slack posts needed, no duplicate workflow.
Scenario: Increase That Requires RM Approval
Marcos needs to raise guidance for Richard from 160 → 200 for RIA work.
The system detects capacity is exceeded.
Guidance request enters “Pending RM Approval” state.
RM receives a notification and approves.
NOS updates guidance and notifies stakeholders automatically.
Audit log reflects both the submission and RM approval steps.

Tasks.title: Fix: Daily Updates Skip Weekends (With Optional Weekend Inclusion)
Tasks.description:
Daily Updates Skip Weekends/Holidays (With Optional Weekend Inclusion)   
As a Project Updater, I want daily updates to skip weekends by default, but allow weekend updates for special projects where weekend activity is required.

Acceptance Criteria
Daily update scheduling automatically excludes weekends by default.
A new project-level checkbox “Include Weekends” controls weekend behavior.
The checkbox is off by default for all projects.
When the checkbox is enabled, daily updates generate on Saturday and Sunday.
When the checkbox is disabled, no updates are expected or flagged as missing on weekends.
Setting can be changed anytime by users with the appropriate permissions.
If a Due Date Falls on a Weekend or US Holiday - then the due date update should push to the following non Weekend/Holiday.
Intended for projects with weekend go-lives, cutovers, deployments, production pushes, etc.
 
Ask Brian - how to test if it's mid week...looking to QA - Faked a holiday

DEV Tasks
 
Data
Create Tables
Country ✅
PersonCountry
Start.End Dates
Holiday ✅
Year
CountryID
Date
Holiday
Description (For Time Entry)
 
Logic
Skip Weekends ✅
Skip Holidays (Start w US)
Would need to update the rule that sets "Status Due Date"
 
UI
New pages in TM App ✅
Holiday Schedule
Highlight Country
See Holidays and Dates
Add Country
 
Security
Weekend Handling Fix
Weekend days (Saturday and Sunday) should not count as late or due for daily updates. ✅
The previous behavior that marked weekends as late was a bug.
New “Includes Weekends” Bit Flag
A new boolean field will be added to the Project table (e.g., includes_weekends). ✅
It will default to 0 (false), meaning weekends are excluded from update requirements. ✅✅
Only admins can toggle this flag if a project truly needs weekend updates (rare cases like critical go-lives).
Due Date / Missed Logic Adjustment
Automated “missed” logic must respect the weekend flag. ✅
If weekends are excluded, due dates will automatically skip Saturday and Sunday. ✅
No late or missed records will be generated for weekend dates.
Next due date should always fall on a weekday (typically Friday or Monday).
UI/UX Update
Add the “Includes Weekends” field to the project setup tab.
Default value = Off.
Only visible/editable by admins.

A “Next Update Due” indicator per project.
A Late/Overdue status/flag when applicable.
P6. System supports Draft and Submitted/Published statuses for weekly updates

Tasks.title: Test Case 01
Tasks.description:
TC-01: All Active Projects Share the Same Weekly Deadline (Monday 5:00 PM EST)
Covers:
 ✔ All active projects share a single standard weekly deadline: Mondays at 5:00 PM EST.
 ✔ The deadline applies to projects regardless of owner, client, or type.
Steps
Ensure there are at least three Active projects:
Project A – Client X – Owner 1 – Type “Implementation”
Project B – Client Y – Owner 2 – Type “Support”
Project C – Client Z – Owner 3 – Type “Internal”
Log in as any user with access to all three projects (e.g., Client Partner or Admin).
Navigate to a view listing all active projects with their update info OR open each project’s details.
Check the update due date displayed for Projects A, B, and C.
Expected Results
ER1: For the current week, all three Active projects show the same due date/time:
“Next Update Due: Monday at 5:00 PM EST” (or equivalent wording).
ER2: The due date does not vary based on project owner, client, or type.

Tasks.title: Test Case 02
Tasks.description:
TC-02: “Next Update Is Due” Indicator Shows Correct Upcoming Monday
Covers:
 ✔ The system automatically shows when the next update is due.
Steps
Set the system date/time to a Wednesday before the upcoming Monday at 5:00 PM EST.
Log in as a Project Updater for Project A (Active).
Navigate to Project A’s overview page.
Expected Results
ER1: A clear indicator is shown, e.g., “Next update due: Monday, [date] at 5:00 PM EST.”
ER2: The date shown corresponds to the next upcoming Monday, not a past one.
ER3: If today is Monday but before 5:00 PM EST, it should show today’s date as the due date.
(You can repeat this with different days of the week if you want to validate edge cases.)

Tasks.title: Test Case 03
Tasks.description:
TC-03: Late/Overdue Flag After Monday 5:00 PM EST With No Update
Covers:
 ✔ Projects missing the Monday deadline are flagged as Late/Overdue.
Steps
Ensure Project A is Active and has no weekly update submitted for the current week.
Set the system date/time to Monday, 5:01 PM EST (1 minute past the deadline).
Log in as Project Updater for Project A.
Navigate to Project A’s overview page and any reporting/portfolio view.
Expected Results
ER1: Project A is clearly flagged as Late or Overdue (badge, icon, label, etc.).
ER2: The “Next Update Due” indicator either:
Shows the current week as overdue, and/or
Indicates next due date while still showing “Overdue” for the missed one (depending on design).
ER3: Any summary or portfolio view of projects also indicates Project A as Late/Overdue.

Tasks.title: Test Case 04
Tasks.description:
TC-04: Meeting the Deadline Clears Late/Overdue Flag
Covers:
 ✔ Reporting is consistent when the update is submitted before the universal due date.
Steps
Ensure Project B is Active with no update yet for the current week.
Set system date/time to Monday, 4:30 PM EST.
Log in as Project Updater for Project B.
Create and Submit/Publish the weekly update for Project B.
Verify Project B’s status at 4:45 PM EST and again at 5:05 PM EST.
Expected Results
ER1: After step 4, Project B is not flagged Late/Overdue.
ER2: At 5:05 PM EST, the current week’s update remains in good standing (no Late/Overdue flag).
ER3: “Next Update Due” is updated to the following Monday at 5:00 PM EST.

Tasks.title: Test Case 05
Tasks.description:
TC-05: Universal Deadline Applies Regardless of Owner/Client/Type
Covers:
 ✔ The deadline applies to projects regardless of owner, client, or type.
Steps
From TC-01 projects (A, B, C), ensure they each have:
Different owners
Different clients
Different project types
Set system time to Monday, 4:50 PM EST.
As each Project Updater (Owner 1 for A, Owner 2 for B, Owner 3 for C), view the project overview.
Expected Results
ER1: All three projects show the same due date/time: Monday 5:00 PM EST for this week.
ER2: No special logic or exception is applied based on owner, client, or type.

Tasks.title: Test Case 06
Tasks.description:
TC-06: Paused/Archived/Inactive Projects Are Excluded From Due-Date Tracking
Covers:
 ✔ If a project is paused, archived, or inactive, it is excluded from due-date tracking.
Steps
Start with:
Project A = Active
Project D = Paused
Project E = Archived (or Inactive)
Set system time to Thursday before the next Monday deadline.
View a portfolio/reporting screen listing all these projects.
Open each project detail page.
Expected Results
ER1: Project A (Active) shows “Next update due: Monday at 5:00 PM EST.”
ER2: Project D (Paused):
Does not show an upcoming due date, or
Clearly indicates “No updates required while project is paused.”
ER3: Project E (Archived/Inactive):
Does not show due dates or Late/Overdue flags.
ER4: Neither D nor E appears in any “Late/Overdue” reporting, even after multiple Mondays pass without updates.

Tasks.title: Test Case 07
Tasks.description:
TC-07: System Reminders Use Universal Due Date
Covers:
 ✔ System reminders or notifications use the universal due date.
Steps
Ensure notifications/reminders are enabled in the test environment (email, in-app, Slack, etc.).
For Active Project A with no update submitted for the current week:
Set system time to Monday, 12:00 PM EST (or whatever reminder window your system uses).
Observe outgoing reminders/notifications for Project A.
Optionally repeat for Project B (another active project) to confirm consistency.
Expected Results
ER1: Reminder explicitly references the universal deadline, e.g.,
 “Your weekly update for Project A is due by Monday at 5:00 PM EST.”
ER2: All Active projects (A, B, etc.) receive reminders keyed to the same Monday 5:00 PM EST deadline.
ER3: Paused/Archived/Inactive projects receive no reminders.

Tasks.title: Test Case 08
Tasks.description:
TC-08: Draft Mode Is Compatible With Universal Due Date
Covers (from Notes):
 ✔ You can work on a draft all week but must submit by Monday at 5 PM EST.
Steps
Ensure Project A is Active.
On Tuesday, log in as Project Updater for Project A and:
Create a weekly update and Save as Draft.
On Thursday, reopen the draft and modify content; save again as Draft.
On Monday at 4:45 PM EST, open the draft and Submit/Publish it.
On Monday at 5:05 PM EST, verify status.
Repeat the scenario but this time do not submit the draft by 5:00 PM EST; check status at 5:05 PM EST.
Expected Results
ER1: Throughout the week, the draft remains editable without affecting Late/Overdue status.
ER2: When submitted at 4:45 PM EST on Monday:
Project is not flagged Late/Overdue.
Next due date moves to the following Monday at 5:00 PM EST.
ER3: When the draft is not submitted by 5:00 PM EST:
Project is flagged Late/Overdue at 5:05 PM EST.
The presence of a Draft alone does not satisfy the due date requirement.

Tasks.title: Fix: LATE SIGN OFFS tab shows no results

Tasks.title: Improve: Update of Person Periods and Capacity Values
Tasks.description:
Original Request
Melissa is looking for an easier way to add or update Person Periods in the Talent Management (TM) app, specifically for users missing 2026 capacity.
 She notes that:

There is currently no clear UI method to add a missing PersonPeriod line item.

Missing capacity numbers negatively impact her RM Availability Report, which relies on accurate forward-looking availability.
 
User Stories
1. Automatic Generation of Person Periods
As a Talent Manager,
 I want Person Periods to be automatically generated for all active individuals whenever new annual periods are created,
 So that capacity planning always includes future years without requiring manual edits per person.
2. Ability to Add Missing Person Periods
As an Admin or Manager,
 I want a way to add missing Person Period entries when necessary,
 So that data gaps do not impact reporting or availability forecasts.
3. Bulk Update or Auto-Population of Capacity
As a Talent Manager,
 I want an efficient way to populate or update capacity values for multiple people at once,
 So that I don’t need to manually adjust each PersonPeriod record individually.

Tasks.title: Add: Slack Reminders for Upcoming & Late Submissions
Tasks.description:
User Story
As a Customer Success Manager (CSM),
I want a Slack reminder posted to the CSM team channel before a submission is due (and again if it becomes late),
So that the team has clear visibility and we reduce individual Slack DM/email spam while still preventing missed deadlines.

Acceptance Criteria
Reminder timing (upcoming):
The system sends a Slack reminder 4 hour before the submission due time.
Reminder timing (late):
If the submission is not completed by the due time, the system sends a Slack reminder indicating it is late.
Notification delivery:
Reminders are posted to the CSM Team Slack channel.
Message content (minimum):
Customer/account name
Due soon vs Overdue
Noise control / deduping:
Only one reminder per item per trigger (one “1-hour before” reminder, one “overdue” reminder), even if jobs retry.
No reminder is sent if the submission is already completed before the trigger time.
Configurability (basic):
Slack channel is configurable (environment setting or admin config), without code changes.

Tasks.title: Add: Project Health page usability and filtering
Tasks.description:
User Story
As a project stakeholder
I want the Project Health page to load with the most relevant projects and metrics by default
So that I can immediately understand current project status without extra setup.

Includes
Default to All Projects
Sort by Latest Updates (descending)
Remove Budget field
Show Actuals (All Time) consistently
Acceptance Criteria
On first load, the page displays all projects with Latest Update sorting applied.
Budget is not shown on the page.
Actuals are displayed as all-time values by default.

****************
Add portfolio filtering by Project Type and Project Lead (with data readiness)
As a project stakeholder
I want to filter and segment the Project Health list by key portfolio dimensions
So that I can focus on the right slice of projects (type and ownership) during reviews.
Includes
Filter by Project Type (Phased / Scaled)
Quick filtering by Project Lead (tiles and/or a dropdown/native filter)
Handling for missing/blank Project Type / Lead values
Optional: programmatic defaulting rules for Project Type to reduce manual cleanup
Acceptance Criteria
Project Type filter supports at least: Phased, Scaled (and a sensible behavior for blanks).
Project Lead segmentation enables fast switching between leads and returning to All Projects.
Filters work together with default sorting (Latest Update) and do not break navigation.
Projects with missing Lead/Type are visible and identifiable (e.g., “Unassigned” / “Unknown”) to support cleanup.
Notes / Dependency
Data cleanup may be required because Project Type is currently often blank.
If implemented, a programmatic default rule may assign Project Type based on existing project fields (e.g., end date + name heuristic).

Tasks.title: Add: Default milestone set by Project Type
Tasks.description:
As a Project Lead / CSM
I want each project to automatically start with a predefined set of milestones based on its Project Type (Phased, Scaled, Support), including the appropriate date fields (Committed/Forecast/Actual vs. Actual-only)
So that milestone tracking is consistent across projects, supports planning visibility, and can be used as an input when making resourcing decisions.

Acceptance Criteria
1) Milestone templates by Project Type
When a project is created (or when Project Type is set/changed), the system can apply a default milestone template for that type.

Phased (tracks Committed, Forecast, Actual):
Kick Off
First Demo
First Users Logged In
Technical Production
End User Production

Scaled (tracks Actual only):
Production Release Notes (created for each period)
SBR (created for each quarter)

Support (tracks Actual only):
Bug Resolution List (created for each period)
SBR (created for each quarter)

2) Date fields match milestone type rules
Phased milestones display and store: Committed Date, Forecast Date, Actual Date
Scaled/Support milestones display and store: Actual Date only
Milestones clearly indicate when a date is missing (e.g., Not set)

3) Milestone creation behavior (avoid duplicates)
Applying a template does not create duplicates if milestones already exist
If Project Type changes, the system follows a safe behavior (e.g., add missing milestones for the new type; do not delete existing milestones)

4) UI placement (Health or Deliverables)
Milestones are visible from the Project Health and/or Deliverables area (final placement TBD), and:
Users can quickly view upcoming milestones
Users can update milestone dates without leaving the project context

5) Resourcing consideration signal
Milestones contribute to resourcing decision support at minimum by:
Surfacing upcoming milestone dates in a way that resource planners can reference
Enabling filtering/sorting for projects with upcoming milestones (e.g., next 30/60/90 days)

Tasks.title: Improve: Include Final Month Actuals When Demand End Date

Actuals for November: $2,100

The invoice total panel on the right shows the previous month’s invoice, which is correct, but the final month’s actuals are not included.

 Even if no new period line is created (since no guidance applies), the system should intuitively include final-month actuals in the summary invoice-to-date amount.

As a Finance or Operations user,
 I want actuals incurred during the final month of a Demand to be included in the invoice total even when no additional period line is generated,
 So that financial visibility is accurate and the total invoiced amount reflects all work performed up to the Demand’s end date.

Clearing the filter to return to the full dataset

Summary totals and any related metrics must also update to reflect filtered data.

Tasks.title: Add: Annual Internal Guidance Configuration

Tasks.title: Add: Reporting Dashboard for Entry Status Tracking

Late entries
On-time entries
Missed entries

Time period (e.g., week, month)

Reporting
Dashboards
Exports (if supported)

Time-sensitive requests

Tasks.title: Add: Pipeline vs Available Resource by Technology

Pipeline Demand Visibility

Monthly hours required

Resource Supply Mapping

Tasks.title: “Missed” logic includes out-of-scope projects
Tasks.description:
Title: “Missed” logic includes out-of-scope projects
Type: Bug
Summary: The “Missed” logic is currently including projects that should be out of scope. This does not impact active / in-scope projects or core functionality. The issue is limited to reporting.
Impact:  Reporting only. Active and in-scope projects are unaffected.
Details:  Projects that are explicitly out of scope are still showing up as “Missed.”
Examples:
Projects where Exclude = 1
Example: Change.org – SOW #5 Project
Projects linked to Demands where Status <> "Active"
Example: WLF Lunar is complete and should no longer be in scope
May also need to check Project Active = 0
Proposed Fix
Delete all existing “Missed” entries
Update the Refresh Jobs and Dashboard View with the following filters:
Exclude projects where Exclude = 1
Exclude projects linked to Demands where Status <> "Active"
Confirm / apply filter where Project Active = 0
Notes: Feels like a straightforward fix once the filters are tightened up.
